entities.summary: The Battle of Columbia was a series of military actions that took place November 24–29, 1864, in Maury County, Tennessee, as part of the Franklin-Nashville Campaign of the American Civil War. It concluded the movement of Lt. Gen. John Bell Hood's Confederate Army of Tennessee from the Tennessee River in northern Alabama to Columbia, Tennessee, and across the Duck River. A Union force under Maj. John M. Schofield skirmished with Hood's cavalry, commanded by Maj. Nathan Bedford Forrest, and fortified a defensive line south of Columbia, but soon withdrew north across the Duck River, abandoning the town.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Battle of Columbia was a pivotal moment in the Franklin-Nashville Campaign, as it forced Lt. Gen. John Bell Hood's Confederate Army to abandon its advance on Nashville, ultimately contributing to the Union victory at the Battle of Nashville and the fall of Atlanta.
